rationale: RegimeSwitcher exploits the fact that on-chain metrics are naturally self-regime-discriminating: at bear bottoms (nupl -30, mvrv -0.35, rhodl 181-400) they all read near zero simultaneously, pulling the composite below 15; at bull tops (nupl 70+, mvrv 4+, rhodl 10k+) they all read 85-100 simultaneously. Rather than dynamic weight switching (not supported by the engine), this is solved through weight concentration and calibrated non-linear mapping. NUPL (24%) and RHODL (18%) dominate because they are the most consistently extreme at both regime poles: RHODL 181 in both the 2018-11 and 2022-11 bear bottoms confirms it as the single clearest capitulation signal, while RHODL 10k-105k at both 2017 and 2021 tops confirms it at the opposite extreme. The RHODL mapping uses a logarithmic ladder — from 181→0 to 105k→100 — because the metric spans 580x in value across regimes. MVRV (18%) gets equal weight to RHODL because it reads negative in BOTH major bear bottoms (2018: -0.35, 2022: -0.20), making it uniquely reliable for regime identification at the cost of being a late indicator. The buy threshold of 22 is deliberately lower than typical configurations to avoid the 'falling knife' problem: in 2018 the index would have scored ~35 in October (nupl~15, mvrv~0.2) BEFORE the final capitulation leg to $3,200 in December when nupl hit -30 and the score fell to ~12 — only below 22 is the on-chain signal strong enough to override the macro downtrend. The pi_cycle_gap (5%) gets a weight boost despite only firing once (2021 April) because when it does fire (gap < 5), it uniquely triggers a score spike above 93 even if other metrics are mixed, ensuring the sell signal is not missed. DCA over 4 tranches at 21-day intervals captures the typical 6-8 week double-bottom pattern observed at both 2018-12 and 2022-11 lows without requiring precise timing of the exact trough.
